Finally, I’m back in Argentina after 40 days of traveling through Russia and Bali.
I had left all my stuff at my friend’s house before I went, but I wasn’t planning on being away for that long. Initially, I thought I’d be gone for 4–15 days or so, but the original plan went off the rails—in a good way. I ended up spending a month in Bali, recharging.

Now I feel more rested, calmer, healthier, stronger, as if I’ve had a proper reset. It’s time to keep working on myself and see how I feel here in Argentina compared to Bali. Like I always say, Buenos Aires feels like a great place to get things done, while Bali is amazing for the body and soul. So I need to try to find some kind of balance.

The original plan to get a passport here in Argentina is no longer realistic, mainly because it’s very unlikely I’ll be able to stay here for four years straight. At the same time, I really enjoy living here. It’s like living in Moscow, but abroad—having that feeling of being a foreigner in a foreign country, which I love. First, because it pushes me and forces me to become better every day. It’s like I’m always at least a little bit outside my comfort zone. Different culture, different language—new things come my way without me having to try, and they make me learn and adapt.

The important thing is not to “fall back” into being overly stressed and chronically sleep-deprived. The plan is to eat mostly carnivore for a month, without restricting calories—basically, to eat as much as I want (following my hunger cues) and see if I gain a lot of weight. The food has to be clean, of course. The idea is that this way of eating is so nutritious and, since the taste variety is limited, I won’t be overeating naturally. Well… the focus is on learning, work, health—yep, keep rolling!
